notes: Identity verified from supplied text: title Determinants of attentional modulation near the hands; Holger Schultheis and Laura A. Carlson; DOI 10.3389/fpsyg.2013.00858; ORIGINAL RESEARCH ARTICLE, published 18 November 2013. Canonical text is an 11-page primary article with methods, results and references, not an abstract or secondary account. No PDF was supplied. Experiment 1 has 62 participants, each completing the within-participant four-posture procedure. Response-time exclusions are trials only (incorrect responses and observations outside each individual/condition mean ±2.5 SD; 7% of trials). No participant exclusion is reported. The participant count is linked to the critical model by this complete within-participant procedure, not derived from degrees of freedom. Exact retained trial count is not reported. Only assigned unfinished fields are populated; all other statistic fields are placeholders. The narrative replication verdict is scoped to the original disengagement modulation. Search rate is defined by the paper as the response-time difference between small and large sets (p. 3). The four-posture interaction includes pray and post, matching the description. Separate tests reported on p. 4 are the posture main effect on overall speed (F < 1; PBIC = 0.92) and lap-versus-screen-only slope comparison (F < 1; PBIC = 0.85); neither supplies the p value for the selected four-posture slope interaction.
